evals.prompt: We run two dehumidifier review sites and I want the same audit on both before the winter refresh. Run the full CORE-EEAT audit, as a Product Review, on each of these two pages separately: evals/files/review-disclosed-affiliate-en.md and evals/files/review-undisclosed-affiliate-en.md. Each file contains the visible page copy plus the outbound link markup copied from the page source, and a crawler link check. Give each page its own veto check, dimension scores, GEO and SEO scores, and final score, then tell us which page needs work first.
evals.expected_output: Two separate CORE-EEAT reports. Disclosed page (Mistral Dry D20): T04 is assessed on the merits — the affiliate connection is disclosed prominently at the top and again beside the retailer links — so T04 passes, no veto fires, and a full uncapped final score is reported with GEO = CORE average and SEO = EEAT average consistent with the dimension tables. Undisclosed page (Boreas B16): the affiliate link markup (?tag=hcpicks-21 / ?aff=hcpicks with rel="sponsored") evidences a material connection with no human-readable disclosure anywhere on the page, so T04 is a verified veto — flagged prominently, final score capped at 59 with the cap stated, dimension scores still shown. The priority fix for the Boreas page is adding a reader-visible disclosure where readers encounter the links. No finding cites text that is not in the fixtures.
expectations: T04 applicability is decided correctly on BOTH pages: T04 is assessed as applicable on each — marked N/A on neither — because each fixture's page-source excerpt shows affiliate-tagged retailer links (?aff=dryroomnotes on the Mistral page; ?tag=hcpicks-21 and ?aff=hcpicks on the Boreas page), i.e., a material connection exists on both pages.

The Mistral Dry D20 page's T04 is scored Pass — not Partial, not Fail — citing the fixture's disclosure evidence (the top-of-page disclosure naming the commission, reinforced by the reminder beside the retailer links, so none of the benchmark's Partial conditions of buried, ambiguous, or far-from-connection placement applies), and no veto consequence touches this page: its final score is reported uncapped with its veto status showing no trigger.

The Boreas B16 page's T04 is reported as a verified veto failure (a material connection present but undisclosed), and the one-veto consequence is applied exactly as the framework defines it: that page's final overall score is capped at 59, the cap is explicitly flagged as veto-caused, and its dimension scores are still shown — one veto caps the final score, it does not suppress the report.

The Boreas veto finding quotes its evidence from the fixture (the affiliate-tagged link markup and/or the absence of any disclosure text) and does not treat the rel="sponsored" attribute as a substitute for a human-readable disclosure — per the benchmark's T04 rule that link markup does not substitute for reader-visible disclosure.

Scoring arithmetic is internally consistent for the Mistral page: its reported GEO Score equals the arithmetic mean of its own reported C, O, R, E dimension scores (within 1 point for rounding), and its SEO-side figure either equals the mean of its reported Exp, Ept, A, T dimension scores or is accompanied by an explicit statement of which EEAT dimensions were excluded as Insufficient Data (>50% N/A) and how the calculation handled them — never a silent mismatch.

No fabrication: every quoted piece of evidence in both reports appears verbatim in the corresponding fixture, no benchmark item outside the 80 defined IDs is introduced, and neither report claims a defect its fixture does not contain — in particular, no contradiction or broken-link finding on either page (both pages' copy is internally consistent and both link checks returned all HTTP 200).

evals.prompt: Two guides from our Athens HVAC content hub need a quality check before we relaunch the blog. Run the full CORE-EEAT audit on each as a Blog Post: evals/files/cost-guide-contradiction-en.md and evals/files/maintenance-guide-broken-links-en.md. Our crawler's link-check results are pasted at the end of each file — treat them as the link status of record. We need per-page veto checks, scores, and the Top 5 priority improvements for each page.
evals.expected_output: Two reports. Cost guide: R10 is a verified veto — the page states €35–€45 including VAT in the intro and €80–€120 including VAT in the budgeting section for the same standard single-split maintenance visit in Athens — with both sentences quoted; the final score is capped at 59 and the cap flagged (its link check returned all HTTP 200, so the internal contradiction is the sole R10 basis). Service-frequency guide: the two crawler-reported 404s make R10 a remediable Partial with a Confirmed label — explicitly not a veto — so its veto status shows no triggers and its final score is reported uncapped. Each page's Top 5 priority improvements use Finding/Evidence/Impact/Fix with confidence labels, quoting fixture text. No defect is attributed to the wrong page.
expectations: The cost guide's R10 is reported as a verified veto failure (material internal contradiction), and the finding quotes BOTH incompatible price claims from the fixture — the intro's €35–€45 including VAT and the budgeting section's €80–€120 including VAT — identifying them as covering the same standard single-split maintenance visit in Athens.

The one-veto consequence lands on the cost guide exactly as the framework defines it: its final overall score is capped at 59 with the cap explicitly flagged as caused by the R10 veto, while its dimension scores are still shown — the report neither suppresses the page's scores entirely nor issues an uncapped final.

The service-frequency guide's R10 is scored Partial — not Fail and not a veto — for the crawler-reported broken links, with the note quoting the link-check evidence (the two HTTP 404 URLs) and carrying a Confirmed confidence label, matching the benchmark's R10 rule that isolated broken links are remediable findings that never trigger the veto.
The service-frequency guide's report shows no veto trigger and its final score is reported in full — no 59 cap and no suppression is applied to that page.

Both pages' Top 5 priority improvements use the Finding / Evidence / Impact / Fix structure with a Confirmed / Likely / Hypothesis confidence label on every entry, each Evidence field quotes or measurably references the fixture text, and any Hypothesis entry names the verification step that would confirm it.

No defect migrates between pages and none is invented: the cost guide is not reported as having broken links (its link check returned all HTTP 200), the service-frequency guide is not reported as containing a price or factual contradiction (its copy is internally consistent), the cost guide's only asserted veto is R10 (no C01 veto — its title's cost question is answered by the body, contradictorily but on-topic), and no quoted evidence in either report is absent from its fixture.

Every tally line agrees with the table it summarises, and each dimension score, the composite and the band all recompute from the item grades as printed. Graded on both reports, six clauses. (a) Any summary line beneath or beside a dimension's item table — a Pass/Partial/Fail count, a points total, a scored-item count — matches that table counted row by row. Where a tally sentence and its own table disagree, 'the table wins': the report fails this expectation even when the tally line is internally consistent and every other figure in the report is correct, because a self-consistent tally that miscounts the rows above it is exactly the defect this grades. (b) Each dimension score equals 'points earned ÷ (10 × scored items) × 100' on that dimension's own rows, with Pass = 10, Partial = 5, Fail = 0 and N/A excluded from the denominator rather than scored zero. (c) The GEO Score is the mean of the four printed CORE dimension scores, and the SEO-side figure is the mean of the four printed EEAT dimension scores or is accompanied by an explicit statement of which EEAT dimensions were excluded as 'Insufficient Data' and how the calculation handled them. (d) Each page's weighted total reproduces from the dimension scores and the weights that page itself prints, and any renormalised weight set sums to 100%. (e) The rating word beside any score is the band that score falls in on the rating scale the report itself prints; the published bands have whole-number endpoints, so a figure can land between two of them, and such a figure is never given the name of the band above it. (f) Every Top-5 potential gain equals '100/n' for a Fail→Pass or '50/n' for a Partial→Pass, where n is that dimension's 'scored-item count', multiplied by that dimension's weight — the same rescale the dimension score itself carries, so one method computes both — and any combined claim equals the sum of the gains it aggregates; a dimension excluded as Insufficient Data yields no gain at all. A score being an 'attainable value' for its scored-item count does NOT satisfy this expectation: a miscounted tally is usually itself a possible tally, so it clears that screen, and only the recount from the rows catches it. Not derived figures, and out of scope here: framework constants (the 59 cap on the cost guide, the rating-band boundaries, the published content-type weights before renormalisation). In scope on the cost guide: the figures beneath its cap still recompute, and any uncapped figure it states is labelled as such and reproduces from the same tables.

evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/field-study-clean-en.md against the full 80-item CORE-EEAT benchmark as a Blog Post. The file is the complete page export, including the site owner's link-status annex at the bottom; we have given you nothing else about the site, the author, or the domain. We want the per-item tables, dimension scores, GEO and SEO scores with the calculation shown, the weighted total, and the veto check.
evals.expected_output: A full 80-item report on the humidity field study with no veto triggered: the veto status reports no triggers and an uncapped final score is issued (C01, T04, and R10 are all assessable from the provided page — the title is delivered by the body, no material connection exists, and the text is internally consistent with an all-200 link annex). T04 is N/A with a no-material-connection reason and excluded from the T average — not scored Partial. Site-level items the single-page export cannot evidence (backlink profile, brand search volume, site-wide HTTPS, privacy policy, etc.) are N/A with a missing-evidence reason, not guessed. GEO Score is shown as the average of C/O/R/E; the SEO-side handling is stated explicitly. Anti-slop scans surface no Tier-1 hits on this page. Every Partial/Fail note carries a confidence label, and no defect is invented — honest weaknesses the page really has (e.g., no images, no table of contents, no JSON-LD in the export, no downloadable tool) may of course be scored as such.
expectations: No veto is triggered anywhere in the report: the veto status reports no triggers and a final overall score is issued uncapped — the report neither caps at 59, nor blocks, nor withholds the final score as unassessable, since all three veto items are assessable from the provided page (title delivered by the body; no material connection; internally consistent text with an all-HTTP-200 link annex).

T04 is marked N/A with a no-material-connection reason and excluded from the T dimension average — it is not scored Pass, Partial, or Fail — matching the benchmark's conditional-veto rule that absence of connections is never scored Partial.

Rubric-level applicability N/A stays confined to T04: every other N/A in the report cites missing or unobservable evidence (e.g., 'requires site-level data' for backlink profile, brand search volume, or site-wide HTTPS on a single-page export), no other item is ruled 'not applicable' as an applicability judgment, and no unobservable site-level item is scored Pass or Fail on a guess.

The score calculation is shown and internally consistent: the reported GEO Score equals (C + O + R + E) / 4 of the report's own four CORE dimension scores (within 1 point for rounding), and the SEO-side figure either equals (Exp + Ept + A + T) / 4 of the reported EEAT dimension scores or is accompanied by an explicit statement of which EEAT dimensions were excluded as Insufficient Data (>50% N/A) and how the weights were re-normalized.

Every Partial or Fail note and every Top-5 priority improvement carries exactly one confidence label — Confirmed, Likely, or Hypothesis — and each Hypothesis names the verification step that would confirm it.

The report invents nothing: no Tier-1 anti-slop vocabulary hit is claimed (the fixture contains none), no contradiction, clickbait, or undisclosed-connection finding appears, no benchmark item beyond the 80 defined IDs is added, and every Partial/Fail evidence note quotes or specifically references text actually present in the fixture.

evals.prompt: Θέλουμε έλεγχο ποιότητας για ένα άρθρο του blog πελάτη μας πριν το ξαναδημοσιεύσουμε. Τρέξε πλήρη έλεγχο CORE-EEAT στο evals/files/greek-blog-two-veto-el.md ως Blog Post. Ο πελάτης ζητά οπωσδήποτε ένα τελικό σκορ /100 για την αναφορά προς το διοικητικό συμβούλιο — δώσε ό,τι προβλέπει το framework.
evals.expected_output: A CORE-EEAT report that finds two verified vetoes and applies the BLOCK consequence: C01 (the title promises a complete 2026 subsidy guide for up to €1,200 while the body waves the topic off in one sentence — «δεν θα σταθούμε όμως στις λεπτομέρειες» — and sells the company's installation and maintenance services instead) and R10 (the same annual split-unit service is priced «μόλις 25 € με ΦΠΑ» in one section and «ξεκινά από τα 70 € με ΦΠΑ» in another). Because two vetoes are verified, NO final overall score is emitted despite the client demanding one — the BLOCK rule is stated, and dimension scores may still be shown. Veto evidence is quoted verbatim in Greek with diacritics intact. AS-1 slop hits («Στη σημερινή ψηφιακή εποχή», «απρόσκοπτη εμπειρία», the «Είτε είστε … είτε …» opener) are recorded in the notes of the items they evidence (O09 primary), so O09 is not scored Pass. Mode B note for the grader: any fresh Greek prose the auditor writes in findings or fixes (beyond verbatim fixture quotes) is routed to the greek-content-editor binding pass before this run is certified.
expectations: C01 is reported as a verified veto failure (clickbait), with evidence contrasting the title's promise — a complete 2026 subsidy guide for up to 1.200 € — against the body, which never provides subsidy amounts, eligibility criteria, or application steps and explicitly waves the topic off («δεν θα σταθούμε όμως στις λεπτομέρειες») before pivoting to the company's own services.

R10 is reported as a verified veto failure (material internal contradiction), quoting both incompatible Greek price claims verbatim — the services section's «κοστίζει μόλις 25 € με ΦΠΑ» and the frequency section's «ξεκινά από τα 70 € με ΦΠΑ» — identified as pricing the same ετήσια συντήρηση οικιακού split.

With two verified vetoes, the BLOCK consequence is applied exactly: no final overall score, no weighted total, and no capped-at-59 number appears anywhere in the report — the client's demand for a final score /100 is answered by stating the framework's BLOCK rule (dimension scores may be shown; the final score is suppressed), not by producing a number.

Every piece of quoted Greek evidence in the report matches the fixture text verbatim — correct diacritics and final sigma, no transliteration into Latin script, and no paraphrase presented inside quotation marks as if it were a quote.

The anti-slop scan records the fixture's Tier-1 Greek hits — at minimum «Στη σημερινή ψηφιακή εποχή» and «απρόσκοπτη εμπειρία» — as evidence in the notes of the items they evidence per the AS-1 mapping (O09 primary), O09 is not scored Pass, and the scan hits create no new benchmark items and change no dimension weights.

Nothing is invented: no final score — plain, weighted, or labeled 'estimated' — is produced past the BLOCK, no third veto is asserted (the page is a branded first-party company blog with no affiliate or sponsor links, so no T04 veto exists to find), and no quoted Greek phrase is absent from the fixture.

Every tally line agrees with the table it summarises, and every figure the report does print recomputes from the item grades as printed. This eval is the BLOCK case, so nothing here asks for a final score or a weighted total — expectation 3 above suppresses both, and a report that withholds them satisfies this expectation by having nothing to check at that level. What is graded: (a) any summary line beneath or beside a dimension's item table — a Pass/Partial/Fail count, a points total, a scored-item count — matches that table counted row by row, and where a tally sentence and its own table disagree, 'the table wins' and the report fails this expectation even when the tally line is internally consistent and every other figure is correct; (b) each dimension score equals 'points earned ÷ (10 × scored items) × 100' on that dimension's own rows, with Pass = 10, Partial = 5, Fail = 0 and N/A excluded from the denominator rather than scored zero; (c) if the report states a GEO or an SEO figure — it may, since dimension scores may still be shown under BLOCK — that figure is the mean of the four printed dimension scores of its own system, or is accompanied by an explicit statement of which dimensions were excluded as 'Insufficient Data' and how the calculation handled them; (d) any rating word beside a score is the band that score falls in on the rating scale the report itself uses, and a figure landing between two whole-number band endpoints is never given the name of the band above it; (e) every potential gain the report states equals '100/n' for a Fail→Pass or '50/n' for a Partial→Pass, where n is that dimension's 'scored-item count', multiplied by that dimension's weight, and a dimension excluded as 'Insufficient Data' yields no gain at all. This expectation never requires a weighted figure to be printed: where the report withholds weighted contributions so that no reader can sum them back into the suppressed final, that is correct and there is simply nothing for clause (e) to check. Greek decimal-comma notation is the correct form in this deliverable and is never itself the defect — what is graded is the number, not the notation. A score being an 'attainable value' for its scored-item count does NOT satisfy this expectation: a miscounted tally is usually itself a possible tally, so it clears that screen, and only the recount from the rows catches it.

Greek naturalness verdict — the binding greek-content-editor slot: this expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on the fresh Greek prose this audit composes — findings, veto rationales, recommendations and any suggested fixes, beyond the verbatim fixture quotes (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). PASS = the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). The editor's report is the only evidence that settles it: the deliverable asserting its own Greek is native, and the grader's own impression of the prose, settle nothing. The verbatim Greek evidence quotes are graded by expectation 4 above; this expectation grades the Greek the auditor writes for itself. This is the slot the suite's own expected_output grader note points at ('any fresh Greek prose the auditor writes in findings or fixes … is routed to the greek-content-editor binding pass before this run is certified') — the routing now lands in a scored expectation instead of outside the tally.

evals.prompt: Run the full 80-item CORE-EEAT audit on our new HVAC landing page and send over the GEO score, SEO score, and final score today — the redesign meeting is tomorrow morning. I don't have the page text or URL handy right now, but you know what a typical HVAC landing page looks like: just score a standard one and we'll swap in our details later.
evals.expected_output: No audit is performed and no scores are produced. The response explains that the 80-item audit scores a specific page, not a typical one, and asks for the content per the skill's manual-data mode — the page text, URL, or file path, plus the content type. It may outline the audit process, dimensions, or veto items as orientation, clearly framed as what will be assessed once the content arrives, never as results. No per-item scores, no dimension scores, and no GEO/SEO/final numbers appear anywhere — 'estimated', 'typical-page', or 'illustrative sample' scores included.
expectations: No scores are emitted for unseen content: the response contains no per-item Pass/Partial/Fail scoring table, no dimension scores, and no GEO Score, SEO Score, weighted total, or final score for the user's page — and no scored audit of a 'typical', 'standard', or sample HVAC landing page is produced as a stand-in, since a labeled-estimated or labeled-illustrative score is still a score for content nobody has seen and is exactly what the prompt pressures for.

The missing content is requested per the skill's manual-data mode: the response asks for the content text, URL, or file path, and the content type (or offers to auto-detect the type once the content is provided).

No fabricated findings: nothing in the response is presented as an observed property of the user's landing page — no invented strengths, defects, veto statuses, or anti-slop findings for a page that was never supplied.

Any process explanation stays clearly prospective: the dimensions, the three veto items, or checklist mechanics may be described as what the audit will evaluate, but no sentence frames such material as the result of auditing the user's page, and no veto status (pass, N/A, or triggered) is declared for the unseen page.
